name: Nino Paid
label: Signal Records
lede: Jacquan Andrews wrote his first songs at eight, spent years in foster care, quit rapping, and came back in 2022 as Nino Paid. One sad-song video later he had a Columbia-backed deal, and two years after that an XXL Freshman cover.

eras.title: Foster care, a false start, a second try
eras.text: Andrews grows up in Prince George's County, Maryland, after his early years in the foster system. He tries music as a teenager under another name, stops, then returns in 2022 as Nino Paid.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nino Paid · The FADER: Nino Paid and his lived-in pain rap
years.h: Jacquan Andrews is born in Landover, Maryland
years.p: By about age four he and his three siblings are in foster care. He and his younger sister are later adopted.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, he and his siblings were removed from their parents by D.C. child services and split into pairs. He describes years of abuse and homelessness before a construction-worker father and a church-cook mother adopted him and his sister.

In the FADER's 2025 profile he talks about a stepfather who has died and about his adoptive mother, whom he calls his mama. He says he imagines his music playing at the family table.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nino Paid · UPROXX: Nino Paid Isn't Afraid Of The Truth On The Chilling Love Me As I Am
years.h: Zeal, the teenage rapper, is retired. Nino Paid takes over
years.p: Andrews put out a single called "Change" as Zeal in August 2017, then stopped. The new name arrives in 2022.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says he began making songs around eight and released "Change" as Zeal on August 9, 2017. In between he ran into trouble: he earned his GED while held at a juvenile detention center in Philadelphia, on robbery and auto theft charges, and later left Prince George's Community College during his first semester.

UPROXX lists his first job as Six Flags, in park services.

eras.title: One video, one deal, one album
eras.text: "Pain & Possibilities" travels far enough to land him a distribution deal with Signal Records, the Columbia and Sony joint venture. His first album follows within eight months.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nino Paid · The FADER: Nino Paid is only going up in new FADER doc
years.h: One video, and Signal Records comes calling
years.p: "Pain & Possibilities" is his first single as Nino Paid. It spreads online almost at once, and Signal signs him to a distribution deal.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the single to August 25, 2023 and ties the Signal deal to its online traction. In the FADER's GEN F documentary he points to the video as his breakthrough and says it went viral right away.

He says his first show was in Atlanta, and that his first show back in the DMV, at Union Stage, sold out.

years.h: Can't Go Bacc is the debut album
years.p: It's out on Signal Records, with "When I Was Young" among its songs. The rest of 2024 goes to singles and features.

years.cap: Nino Paid in Prince George's County, Maryland, 2024
years.src: Pitchfork: Quiet Days in Maryland With Nino Paid · Stereogum: Yhapojj Moshpit (Feat. Nino Paid)
years.h: Pitchfork sends Alphonse Pierre to Maryland
years.p: The August 2, 2024 profile calls Nino the introspective new star of DMV rap. Three weeks later he guests on [[Yhapojj|50931a9d-08af-4012-8dae-ecef04e51bf3]]'s "Moshpit".
years.xp:
The Pitchfork story, by Alphonse Pierre, is titled "Quiet Days in Maryland With Nino Paid, the Introspective New Star of DMV Rap."

Stereogum's post on "Moshpit" (August 21, 2024) has the Alabama rapper [[Yhapojj|50931a9d-08af-4012-8dae-ecef04e51bf3]] and Nino both sounding casual and in control over a bass-heavy, chiming beat.

eras.title: Love Me As I Am, and then everyone is watching
eras.text: A second album, a first tour and an XXL Freshman spot all arrive in one year. So does an arrest in July.

years.src: The FADER: Nino Paid Love Me As I Am review · UPROXX: Nino Paid Isn't Afraid Of The Truth On The Chilling Love Me As I Am
years.h: Eighteen songs in 36 minutes about what success costs
years.p: Love Me As I Am has guests and producers including Tommy Richman, PlaqueBoyMax and JRipey. "Joey Story" is about a friend's suicide.
years.xp:
The FADER's Jordan Darville called it a record about the ambivalence of success, and "Tears in the Hotbox" one of the best emo-rap songs in years. He also notes the more commercial-leaning tracks "Try Me," "Cooln" and "Tyreek Hill."

Nino told UPROXX the album is "everything I been thru and everything in between."

years.src: The FADER: Nino Paid and his lived-in pain rap · Wikipedia: Nino Paid
years.h: First tour: Chicago, Brooklyn, Atlanta, Toronto
years.p: The Love Me As I Am Tour runs four dates. His manager is Prez K of Hustle Firm Entertainment.
years.xp:
The FADER's March 2025 profile, by Kaila Philo, lists the cities on the way. Wikipedia counts the run as four dates.

He says in the profile that he isn't sad all the time, and that he doesn't like following people just because everyone else is going there.

years.cap: Nino Paid, XXL 2025 Freshman Class portrait, June 2025
years.src: HotNewHipHop: Rich In Rome · Wikipedia: Nino Paid
years.h: XXL names him one of its twelve Freshmen
years.p: He'd already made Pigeons & Planes' 25 Artists to Watch and played Lyrical Lemonade's Summer Smash. In August he teams with fellow freshmen ian and [[Lazer Dim 700|95b0d5b3-2815-4ffc-9bfe-2ace8300b463]] on "Rich In Rome".
years.xp:
HotNewHipHop says ian, Lazer Dim 700 and Nino were all in the 2025 XXL Freshman class. The song has a Cardo Got Wings beat and a video shot in Italy, and it follows their first pairing, "Get To It" in May.

Wikipedia says Nino's XXL selection came in June 2025.

years.src: HotNewHipHop: Maryland Rapper Arrested · Wikipedia: Nino Paid
years.h: Arrested in Maryland, released the next day
years.p: Wikipedia says the charge was vehicle theft and that Nino was released on his own recognizance on July 25.
years.xp:
HotNewHipHop, relaying an XXL report on July 26, said the U.S. Marshals Service made the arrest and that no charges had been made public at the time.

Wikipedia, which has him released on July 25, describes the charges as vehicle theft.

eras.title: Somewhere Over the Rainbow
eras.text: Rolling Loud, a new link-up with the Chicago producer Bugg, and a third album that Pitchfork counts among the year's top-rated.

years.src: The FADER: 18 rappers we can't wait to see at Rolling Loud
years.p: The FADER lists him among 18 rappers it can't wait to see, and points to "Old Me" and "Tomorrow Will Be Better," both with millions of streams.

years.src: The FADER: Chicago producer Bugg is locking in with the hardest rappers · The FADER: Bugg does it all, from painting to producing
years.h: Chicago producer Bugg builds "WYM?" around an organ line
years.p: The FADER hears an unusually warm organ over shimmering chords, and Nino Paid flowing as perfectly as ever.
years.xp: The FADER's Bugg feature includes a video for "WYM?" with Nino in it. In a later FADER piece, on September 16, Bugg says he is working on more music with him.

years.cap: Nino Paid at the FADER offices, June 12, 2026
q: I never really thought about my life after my 20s. Like ever.
years.src: The FADER: Nino Paid wants to carry the torch for DMV rap
years.h: Somewhere Over the Rainbow makes Pitchfork's top-rated list for 2026
years.p: The third album is out August 4. The FADER says his pen "has only sharpened" in the year and a half since Love Me As I Am.
years.xp:
In the FADER's video interview, he says he wants to carry the torch for DMV rap. He talks about depression, the deaths around him, a period of heavy drug use he says he came out of, and getting back in touch with his biological mother.

Asked about the future, he tells the FADER he had never thought about life after his twenties.
